title: Should Dell Stock Be Part Of Your Portfolio?
detail:
Should Dell Stock Be Part Of Your Portfolio?
Trefis Team
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 1:00 PM MDT 3 min read
SPGI
HPE
DELL
HPQ
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Dell Technologies (DELL) stock returned about 297% over the past twelve months, against about 16% for the S&P 500. Buyers appear to be betting on its AI servers, but Dell offers a second reason to look. Dell has cut its share count by 11.7% in three years, from 738 million to 652 million, so each share owns a larger slice of the company. So what has that shrinking share count been worth to a shareholder?

What Have Dell's Buybacks Added To Each Share?

Earnings per share has grown about 6.6 percentage points a year faster than Dell's profit. Over three years, net income grew 81.5% a year while earnings per share grew 88.1% a year. The difference is the share count: the same profit is now split among fewer shares.

Most of that growth still came from the profit itself, which rose from $1.9 billion to $11.4 billion over those three years.

Over the last twelve months, Dell spent $8.38 billion on buybacks, after subtracting the stock it issued as pay. That equals 2.4% of its $355.5 billion market value. Each share now owns a larger slice, but what that slice is worth still depends on the stock price.

Dell Runs On Thin Margins And Supplier Credit

Dell is a hardware company with an operating margin of 9.6%, against 18.6% for the S&P 500, and that business funds the buybacks. Dell runs partly on its suppliers' credit: it owes suppliers 2.3 times what it holds in inventory. That suggests Dell often sells its hardware before it has paid for the parts.

AI servers are now a large part of what Dell sells. On its September 1, 2026 call, management said Dell booked $60.9 billion in AI server orders in fiscal Q2 2027 and recognized $16.4 billion in AI server revenue.

Can Dell Keep Buying Back Shares At This Pace?

Not from free cash flow alone, based on the figures for the last twelve months. Dell's free cash flow of $8.56 billion (operating cash flow minus capital spending) covered about 80% of the $10.68 billion it paid out: $9.11 billion on buybacks, before netting out stock pay, and $1.57 billion in dividends.

In fiscal Q2 2027, Dell bought 9.5 million shares at an average of $401 each. The stock closed at $552.29 on October 5, 2026, so Dell gets fewer shares for the same money.

What Would Stop Dell's Buyback?

Dell's buyback depends on the profit it earns, and management's latest forecast came with a caution. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $192 billion at the midpoint, from $167 billion, on the September 1 call. Yet it also said it would not expect every benefit behind the quarter's infrastructure margin to continue at this level, though it sees structural improvements in the business. It also said DRAM memory chips remain in short supply.

title: What Are Palantir Stock Bulls Not Worried About?
detail:
What Are Palantir Stock Bulls Not Worried About?
Trefis Team
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:34 AM MDT 4 min read
PLTR
^GSPC
GOOG
SNOW
SPGI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) stock has returned 46% over the three months through October 5, 2026, against 3.9% for the S&P 500. Buyers at this price appear to expect the company's sales to businesses to keep growing as fast as they have. But Palantir is no longer alone in chasing those customers, and its own management described one such contest on its latest earnings call. So who is Palantir now up against?

Palantir Now Competes With The AI Labs

Palantir is up against the labs that build the large AI models, and those labs now want the same corporate customers. Management raised the subject on the August 3 call for the second quarter of 2026. It told investors that a shift in AI models the company had warned about for years "is now here."

Management also gave an example. A major tech company had tested one of those labs, and the lab's deployment team, against Palantir's AI platform. Palantir won, and the work became a contract worth $10 million a year.

Palantir uses the labs' models as well, so the labs are both a supplier and a rival. The Information reported on September 14, 2026, that Palantir was among large technology companies that could restrict or stop using advanced AI models. Those companies want Anthropic and OpenAI to guarantee that the companies' intellectual property will not be misused.

How Much Of Palantir's Revenue Comes From Companies?

Companies supplied 46% of Palantir's revenue in fiscal 2025, or $2.1 billion from its Commercial segment. Commercial sales grew 60.0% that year, faster than the 53.1% growth of the Government segment.

The U.S. part of that business is growing fastest. Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue was $764 million in the second quarter of 2026, up 149% from a year earlier. Management forecasts more than $3.424 billion from that business in 2026, which would be growth of at least 134%.

Palantir's share price leaves little room for that growth to slow more than management expects. Buyers pay about $74 for each dollar of Palantir's sales over the past twelve months, against about $3 for the S&P 500. The shares are also about 9% below their 52-week high, so the price appears to assume the labs will not slow Palantir down.

Is Palantir Losing Customers To The AI Labs?

No, there is no sign of it in the customer numbers Palantir reported for the second quarter. Palantir had 653 U.S. commercial customers at the end of the second quarter of 2026, up 35% from a year earlier. It also signed U.S. commercial contracts with a total value of $2.132 billion in that quarter, up 153% from a year earlier.
